text: If I can make pads at or around a ten thousand dollar build-out, with the water and electrical tie-ins included, it could immediately be rented to a dome owner for what?
Five hundred, a thousand, fifteen hundred a month.
At the high end it pays itself back inside a year, no contest.
And there is nothing there to degrade to begin with, so it is easily a ten-year-plus infrastructural commodity.
On the income side the lease is most of it.
The utility margin is a cent or two a unit, and that is payment for metering and paperwork rather than a second rent.
Here it comes to about ten dollars a month.
And payback is on net, after management, tax and insurance.
Payback on gross is a brochure number.
